rappel_detail.notes: First bolted station reached after downclimbing/simul-climbing the upper West Ridge from the true summit; single 60m rope.
hazards: The traverse to reach it is the ultra-exposed ridge crest, with loose rock and gravel over the ledges
rappel_detail.station: Reached by downclimbing and simul-climbing the exposed upper West Ridge crest west from the true summit. The first bolted station is the obvious one just west of the summit - it is the one anchor on this descent nobody reports having trouble finding.

rappel_detail.notes: Second of three further rappels down the north/northwest side, interspersed with short downclimbs and a traverse back to the ridge crest.
hazards: Multiple abandoned tat anchors in the same gully make it easy to commit to the wrong descent line
Rappelling straight down from station 1 takes you past the correct station
rappel_detail.station: The station parties lose. It is not in the fall line below the first - look out to skier's left before committing to a rappel direction. Several old tat-marked stations are scattered through this gully and compete for attention; the correct continuation is the bolted pair, since the whole line was rebolted with chain anchors in 2010.

rappel_detail.notes: Continues down the north/northwest side of the upper ridge.
hazards: Two southwest-facing gullies below the flat section look like the way down and are not - parties are regularly drawn into them. Bypass both and stay with the crest and the south-side ledges
rappel_detail.station: Below the upper rappels the ridge flattens out. The continuation is down the crest and then onto third-class ledges on the south side of the ridge; the next bolted station sits above the large dihedral that dominates this part of the west side.

rappel_detail.notes: Final of the four rappels; below it, downclimb loose exposed 3rd-class terrain and cross a cairned scree bowl back to the boulder field and approach trail.
hazards: Off the ropes it is easy to drift too far skier's left and cliff out. Traverse right, pick up the cairn across the large scree bowl, then zig-zag down to the boulder field and the approach trail
rappel_detail.station: The last bolted station takes you down the dihedral itself and onto the upper scree slopes.

set.rappels: From the summit, about 4 single-rope rappels from bolted chain anchors down the West Ridge (some parties count 5), or twelve or more reversing the buttress. Two half-rope rappels into notches on the lower ridge extension are part of the climb itself.
set.rappel_count_note: This is the standard, faster West Ridge descent on a single 60 m rope, and it is given as either four or five rappels. A 2024 South Buttress party counted four: two off the summit area down the gully, then one above the big dihedral and one down it. Others count five: two down to the flat part of the ridge, then three more off bolted anchors from the third-class ledges on the south side. The difference is how much of the crest between them a party downclimbs, not a disagreement about the anchors - all of them are bolted chain stations (ASCA rebolted 2010). Reversing the South Buttress directly instead takes 12 or more single-rope rappels on mixed bolt, tat and tree anchors and takes considerably longer.
